questions.prompt: You are studying a reference ad frame by frame. Which note will help you most when you make your own?
options: It looks professional and the colours all feel very modern
A new shot every three seconds, text building word by word
The music is trending and the video has lots of views
It was clearly made by a big agency with a large budget
questions.explanation: Write what the video actually does, in things you can copy: pace, how text appears, how the camera moves. "Professional" gives you nothing to build.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest hook for a 30-second cake ad?
options: Hi everyone, welcome back to Amaka's Bakes page
Did you know we make the best cakes in all of Lagos?
Amaka's Bakes: quality cakes for every occasion
She forgot the cake. It's 1pm and the party is at 6.
questions.explanation: A hook is the thing your viewer is already thinking, in the first two seconds. Greetings, brand names and "Did you know" give them a reason to scroll on.

questions.prompt: What single change most improves how much an AI video shot looks like your real product?
options: Starting the shot from a real photo of your real product
Adding more adjectives like stunning and cinematic
Asking for the highest quality mode on every attempt
Generating the whole 30-second ad in one single generation
questions.explanation: Start from a real image. Words alone get you a cake. Your photo gets you your cake.

questions.prompt: You have Google Flow's free daily credits. What is the best way to use them?
options: Save them all up for a week, then make one long video
Use the high-quality mode for every shot you try out
Draft each shot in the fast mode, change one thing each time
Repeat the same prompt again and again until one looks right
questions.explanation: Fast mode costs a fifth of the high-quality mode, and free credits do not roll over. Draft cheaply, change one thing between attempts, and pay only for the shot you know you need.

questions.prompt: Which of these crosses the honest line in a UGC-style ad?
options: You talking to your phone camera about your own product
Hands cutting your real cake, filmed in your own kitchen
An AI actor saying "I ordered this and loved it"
A real customer review, shown as text, with permission
questions.explanation: An AI person must never pretend to be a customer. That is a fake testimonial. The other three are honest.

questions.prompt: Most people watch short videos with the sound off. What does that mean for your ad?
options: Every spoken line needs captions that are easy to read
Music matters more than the words, so pick a trend
The voiceover should be louder than in a normal video
Keep every video under ten seconds so no one gets bored
questions.explanation: If it only works with sound, it does not work for most viewers. Caption every spoken line, big and clear of the app's buttons.

questions.prompt: You want to use an AI voice in an ad that sells your product. What do you need?
options: Any voice from the free plan, since free means allowed
A famous person's voice, cloned so it sounds familiar
A voice from a video you found online, sped up a little bit
A plan with a commercial licence, cloning only your voice
questions.explanation: ElevenLabs' free plan has no commercial licence. And only ever clone your own voice, or one you have written permission to use.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to brief Claude Code for a motion graphic in Remotion or HyperFrames?
options: Ask for a nice, modern animated intro for my brand
Describe the movement beat by beat, with frame timings
Send the logo and let it pick whatever looks best
Ask for the whole video, then fix everything at the end
questions.explanation: Describe movement, not results: what arrives when, how text builds, where the cuts land. Then approve a scene-by-scene plan before it builds.

questions.prompt: Why keep every timing, colour and piece of text in one config file?
options: So you can change them without touching the animation
Because the finished video will not render at all without one
So the video file comes out smaller for your phone
Because Claude Code cannot edit more than one file
questions.explanation: One file for everything you might change means next month's version, or a new price, takes minutes instead of a rebuild.

questions.prompt: You are editing a talking video in CapCut. What should you lay down first?
options: The music, so the edit follows the beat of the song
The captions, so you know where each line will sit
The voice, since it sets the timing for everything
The AI shots, since they took the longest to make
questions.explanation: The voice sets the timing. Cut it tight first, then fit the other shots and the captions around it.
